annotations.title: Does this agent have a business (paid)

description: Does this agent have a BUSINESS, and can any of it be demonstrated? Six questions an investor, a marketplace or an operator actually asks, each answered separately: are the addresses paying it really independent customers; is revenue growing or shrinking; how much is repeat custom; how many of those payments can be shown to have bought anything; what does it cost to run and to whom; and if it has several addresses, can the link be DEMONSTRATED or is it an unconfirmed assumption. Measured on two live agents: one takes $2,388 a month from 4,772 payers of whom 97% are repeat, the other $932,414 from 7,220 payers of whom 12% are — two completely different businesses that a counterparty count reports identically. THERE IS NO SCORE over the six, deliberately: a number would average "thousands of addresses paid this" against "we hold no delivery record at all", and the second is a statement about US. Four things the data invites and this refuses: an ADDRESS is not a customer (one customer can hold twenty); a PAYMENT is not a delivery (the busiest agents settle on rails that carry money without carrying a job, so "no delivery record" there is our reach and not a finding); a SHARED FUNDER is not an identity (an exchange funds thousands of strangers), so a link is published as demonstrated or as merely co-occurring and the second is never promoted; and a COST we cannot see is not a cost that is not there. PAID.
